new.n: Murdered stranger's gold, Mount Vernon ghost village below Minneiska
new.pl: Mount Vernon townsite, sec. 2 T108N R9W, on the Mississippi about a mile below Minneiska. Pin is the 1867 plat village point; the hotel lot and the bluff spot are not placed.
new.v: $40,000 said buried up the bluff, or $8,000 in the hotel cellar (legend)
new.st: In the early 1850s Stephen Burns built one of the finest hotels in the section at Mount Vernon, headquarters for a river stage line; a village of about two dozen homes grew around it and crimes gave it a bad name. One night a wealthy stranger vanished after a quarrel in a gambling house; all versions agree he was murdered. Some said he had crept up the bluff and buried $40,000 beforehand, others that $8,000 lay buried in the hotel cellar. In 1882-83 the founder's son-in-law dug two weeks in the old cellars, mostly at night, returned the next year, then sued for the townsite; others dug the cellars too and found nothing. Minneiska absorbed the village when the Milwaukee road came; by 1914 only ragged lots in a pasture remained, where the river light-tender who told the tale had built his driftwood "castle".
new.t: Legend only. The 1867 plat gives the townsite; find the hotel lot on the plat page and check the 1938 aerial for cellar depressions; the bluff behind is the other named spot. Pasture, private: permission first; look-only until ownership is known.
src: Wabasha County Herald, 10 Dec 1914, p. 7, 'Man of the River… Still Hunted on His Land in Minneiska' (reprinted from the Winona Independent; MNHS newspaper hub doc d43a5ec6-590e-43b7-b4ab-93b95604e90f/mnhi0031/1H0YUO5B/14121001)
